svg.aria-label: Jenkins-Lens — Multi-Agent AI Failure-Analysis and Remediation for a FAILED or UNSTABLE Jenkins build. A red build from any project or pipeline across the gtsci and dacci instances, triggered by a post-failure hook, a webhook, MCP chat or the CLI, is analysed by ten agents in four phases. Phase one, LOCATE: LogFetcher windows the console to the failure region; the Upstream Tracer walks the gtsci trigger chain; the Downstream Tracer crosses into the T7 migration jobs on dacci. Phase two, DIAGNOSE: Diagnostics names the root cause with quoted evidence across sixteen categories; the False-Positive Detector decides whether the red build is genuine with a deterministic 0 to 100 percent score, emitting one verdict — TRUE POSITIVE, INCONCLUSIVE or FALSE POSITIVE — plus a probability. Phase three, PRESCRIBE: ActionSpec writes an ordered, gated action plan; the Reviewer runs two independent critic passes and can send the analysis back with REVISE in a bounded self-correcting loop. Phase four, ACT and NOTIFY: the Remediator is the only write-capable agent and acts only on APPROVE plus a human gate, dry-run by default; the Notifier always reports to Teams, email and the Jenkins build description. The Orchestrator, the tenth agent, coordinates all four phases and an orchestration crash never changes the build result. The outcome is one evidence-grounded verdict with the root cause, quoted evidence and an ordered fix.
svg.title: Jenkins-Lens — ten agents, four phases (Locate · Diagnose · Prescribe · Act & Notify), one verdict — for a failed or UNSTABLE Jenkins build
